Rio Grande Valley Graduation Acceleration for Talented Engineering Students (RGV-GATES)
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
The Rio Grande Valley Graduation Acceleration for Talented Engineering Students (RGV-GATES) program will provide scholarships to academically talented and financially needy engineering students to accelerate their graduation from the ABET-accredited Engineering at The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV) located in South Texas with a highly-concentrated Hispanic population.
From 2020-2025, the RGV-GATES program will fund, on average, 14 engineering scholarships every academic year to support academically promising students as they complete their undergraduate engineering degrees in a timely manner. Five cohorts of engineering students will be supported as they progress towards graduation, including one 2-year cohort, two 3-year cohorts, and two 4-year cohorts [Table 1]. Each cohort is considered complete once it reaches the end of its fourth year. The program will serve a total of 23 unduplicated students, including 11 recent high school graduates, and graduate 21 of them with bachelor’s degrees during the period of the program.
The mission of the program is to retain and graduate UTRGV engineering students within four years (or two years for students starting with an associate degree) of matriculation by providing an environment that supports them with college and engineering readiness, academic advising, peer and faculty mentoring, and assistance in the use of university resources.
Scholarships are to be awarded on the basis of both need and merit. The program aims to hold all participating students to high academic standards. Scholarship recipients must take 15 credit hours each semester and maintain a 3.0+ semester grade point average (GPA). The RGV-GATES program will enable a well-rounded student experience to promote learning and engagement beyond the classroom while maintaining rigorous academic expectations that compel students to maintain momentum toward timely degree completion. All scholarship recipients must apply for the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) each spring to maintain their eligibility in the program.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Machine Learning based Microwave Glucose Concentration Detection
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: Non-invasive microwave measurement methodologies have attracted broader attention and studies inrecent years for the development of convenient and effective blood glucose monitoring. The 3-7 GHzmicrowave frequencies have enough penetration depth and are known to be effective to the dielectricchange led by the variation of the glucose concentration in human blood. The current state of theexploration in this area is mostly focused on the deterministic measurement of dielectric parameters ofglucose inclusive solution based on various Debye relaxation models, or the directly measured S11/S21scattering signals to try to correlate them to the glucose concentration level. Though the studies haveindicated that glucose level variation does produce a definite change in dielectric properties, the glucoselevel within the human physiological range is only a few hundred mg/dL (typically 60-700 mg/dL). Mostreported approaches still cannot accurately correlate the dielectric parameters or direct scattering signalswith the small variation of glucose concentration level. Two major challenges need to be broken for thedeterministic technologies: signals from the targeted blood vessel are usually deeply weakened by thenoise signals from the surrounding tissues in the in vivo scenario, and correlation between dielectricparameters or scattering signals and glucose concentration is non-linear and affected by various factorslike human body physical difference and temperature, and physically unclear.We propose an alternative approach to take advantage of machine learning classification fed by the bigdata sets collected by the non-invasive microwave sensor. The proposed three-year project aims to 1)develop a non-invasive microwave sensing system to monitor and collect the real-time scattered signalsfrom the targeted blood vessel; and 2) to develop machine learning based statistical recognitiontechnique for glucose concentration detection.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Non-invasive real-time microwave sensing of blood glucose concentration
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
The proposed project aims to investigate and develop a non-invasive microwave sensing system for real
time blood glucose concentration detection. Success of the project will not only benefit to those
diagnosed type-1 and type-2 diabetes patients who need constant detection of their blood glucose level,
but will also dramatically benefit to those potential pre-type-2 diabetes people that constant monitoring
of their glucose level is of equal importance. Most of the studies on the non-invasive detection of
glucose concentration are in vitro test only focusing on the glucose solution alone. The proposed project
aims at in vivo non-invasive microwave detection of glucose concentration with interfering noises from
the surrounding tissues. Major challenges have been predicted, including the interfering noises from the
other tissues and the temperature effect. And we have planned the innovative strategies to overcome
both. This project will develop both determinate and artificial neural network (ANN) statistical methods
for the recognition of glucose concentration, to take the advantage of the self-evolutionary nature of
the artificial neural network algorithm and reduce the detection variance from the interfering noise.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Don't Touch That! Assessment of Fear and Likelihood of Purchase Among College Students Using Scalp Recorded EEG Activity
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
1. What is the purpose of your study?
Answer
Record electrical activity from participants brain using scalp recorded electroencephalogram (EEG) to access fear of a food product due to possible adverse effect on human body and the effect of that fear on the purchase likelihood of that product. EEG will be used to validate the self accessed ratings provided by the participant.

Many factors influence food choice and consumption behavior (Koster 2009), fear is one of them (Laros and Steenkamp 2004). Past studies have shown fear appeals concerning genetically modified food (Laros and Steenkamp 2004), consumers’ fear (neophobia) towards food technologies (Verneau et al. 2014), and knowledge of fear and genetically modified food (Boccia et al. 2018). However, studies about food choice motivated by fear have not yet been examined through neuroscientific methods. In this study, we are interested in measuring the level of fear of consumers with regards to food choice when the food in question lacks safety for consumption.

The purpose of this study is not only to measure consumers’ fear level but also try to identify consumer awareness or knowledge in consumer decision-making process in their food purchase intentions. In applying neuroscientific methods to measure the level of fear the effectiveness of different marketing strategies may be evaluated through consumers observing stimuli depicting different types of food (Khushaba et al. 2012). N. Masood et al (2019) investigated EEG patterns for dual-stimuli induced human fear emotional state [1]. They have used two types of stimulus, one is self-recalling of a fearsome event and the other one video clips from horror movies. The authors have employed common spatial pattern (CSP) as preprocessing method to select optimal

EEG channels that will provide best separability of the types of task also called as class and linear discriminant analysis (LDA) as a classifier for the experiment. Emotiv EPOC has been used for EEG data collection from 15 young healthy participants. The experiment was divided into two-part, part one is designed for self-induced stimulus where the subject was asked to recall an event that induces fear in them, part two is for movie clips-based stimulus.

The target was to study whether different stimulus for the same emotional state shows any correlation. The authors have employed 6 bandpass filter for 6 frequency ranges (delta 1-3 Hz, theta 4-7 Hz, alpha 8-13 Hz, low gamma 31- 50 Hz, high gamma 50-100 Hz, whole EEG range 1-100 Hz). ICA was employed to remove independent components with large weights over frontal or temporal areas, together with corresponding temporal courses showing eye movement or muscle movements were removed. CSP was employed to extract features and finally, LDA was used to classify self-induced vs video-induced fear states. The average accuracies were in the range of 54.86 to 72.74 for different frequency band signals.

CONGRANT.TITLE: Study and Develop of an Innovative Non-Destructive Broadband Chirped Pulse Sensor for Chemical/Biological Trace Gas Detection
CONGRANT.AWARDORG: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
The proposed project aims to study and develop the chirped pulse microwave sensor for chemical and
biological trace gas detection. Potential detectable species include automobile gas emission detection,
poisonous and pollution gases, etc. Many molecules have strong and characteristic rotational transitions in
the microwave frequency region. The relative long wavelength of microwave radiation allows it to
propagate further away than infrared radiation. The microwave technique is known to be highly sensitive
to detect this kind of radiation. These properties make spectroscopic sensing of chemical species highly
feasible in this frequency range. We propose to study the principle of the concept of an innovative
portable microwave sensor that utilizes the newly developed chirped pulse technique in microwave
spectroscopy to allow unambiguous determination of a wide range of chemical and biological
gases/species simultaneously.

CONGRANT.ABSTRACT: A frequency domain analysis was used to perform a comparative study of microwave complex dielectric permittivity on different concentration glucose samples. The results obtained were presented in several conferences in the state of Texas and Arizona. Our research was expanded to look for potential bio-markers in the blood stream that can be analyzed with our method.  The efforts will be focused in improving our measurement system and identify one bio-marker for the detection of disease.

DURIP:    Build a wind-riding small drone with morphing wings for multi-agent collaborative learning
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
We propose a solution to kill two birds with one stone: develop a morphing wing for drones to ride winds and save battery life. We will mimic bat wings to achieve desired aerodynamic performance through a simple, light, and easy-to-maneuver mechanical design; artificial muscle fibers will replace traditional motors for actuation.  We vision that the drone can extend its wings to glide like a bird when wind is favorable. When wind is not favorable, the wings will be stretched in. With increased flight time, small drones are suitable for real world applications. 
Furthermore, we propose to enable the intelligence of drones by developing algorithms in computer vision, target recognition and multi-agent collaborative learning. Our goal is to explore the low space (<400m altitude) where we see countless applications directly benefiting human life: photography, transportation, surveillance, etc.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: CPW Integrated Microstrip Array for Three-Dimensional Microwave Imaging
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Development of an effective, compact and wideband microwave antenna array is an important issue for portable microwave imaging systems in biomedical applications. Typical imaging systems have a complicated topology with tangled array-cable connections. In this paper, a 2.8-6.0 GHz coplanar waveguide (CPW) connected microstrip antenna array is developed for three-dimensional (3-D) microwave imaging applications. Array elements are connected and controlled by the RF switches, resulting as a whole, low-cost and clean structure with manipulation convenience. Unique approaches are considered in the design, namely, low signal loss on the CPW transmission line, wide bandwidth and size miniaturization. The simulation and measured results indicate that the antenna array demonstrates satisfactory performance while largely reducing the system complexity.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Development of a Polyimide-Based Flexible Antenna
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: Proceedings of 2013 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and URSI Radio Science Meeting
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT:
Last decade has seen more and more flexible and wearable electronics developed. Research progress in this area has resulted in flexible microelectronic and portable wireless communication design (Y. Sun & A. Rogers, Adv. Mater., 2007). In this paper, a flexible microstrip antenna is designed and optimized for biomedical microwave detection applications. Based on the study on medium-dependent wavelength and attenuation constants of various constituents of the human body, an operating frequency band between 3.2 to 8.5 GHz is chosen for the amtenna. The spectrum locates in the non-ionizing radiation, and the hardware is relatively inexpensive. A copper-clad polyimide  laminate, Pyralux AP  from DuPont, is chosen as the flexible microwave laminate. This material has excellent electrical and mechanical properties, making it ideal for multilayer flex antenna design. 

One of the technical challenges is how to balance the flexibility with the satisfactory antenna performance(operating frequencies, return loss, and radiation pattern change due to flex). Microstrip pattern is well designed and tested under different bending angles. The thickness of the laminate has a thickness of 10 mil, with the consideration of flexibility while maintaining fair antenna performance compared to the flat antenna design. Effect of laminate thickness to both flexibility and antenna characteristics is also demonstrated and explained.

INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: The 28th Annual Symposium of the Antenna Measurement Techniques Association (AMTA)
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Nowadays the demand for multi-band performance devices that can stay in the palm of the hand has become more compelling. In this light, a device that can offer both features at the same time is extremely prized. In this paper the advance in antenna design using non-conventional material with the objective of size reduction is carried out. A dual-band microstrip antenna resonating at 1.8GHz and 2.4 GHz has been designed and simulated using the Ansoft HFSS package. Pyrolytic boron nitrite (PBN), which has an anisotropic dielectric with a relative electric permittivity represented by a diagonal tensor, is adopted as the substrate of the designed antenna to achieve the size reduction while maintaining the antenna performance. The design is then compared with the one that uses isotropic substrate (i.e. RO4003). Comparison shows that the introduction of such a non-conventional medium approximately allows the antenna size to be reduced by 13% while maintaining almost the same electromagnetic performance. Issues about size reduction and frequency shifting are further presented and discussed in the paper.

PRESENT.NAME: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and North American Radio Science Meeting
PRESENT.TITLE: Microwave based Glucose Concentration Determination using Machine Learning
PRESENT.ABSTRACT: Abstract— Non-invasive blood sugar measurement attracts more and more attention in recent years, given the increase in diabetes-related complications and inconvenience in the traditional ways using blood droplets. In this paper, we present a study on the use of machine learning algorithms to determine glucose concentration based on the microwave scattering parameters (S11) measured on the glucose solution with various concentrations. Dielectric parameters were extracted appropriately based on the modified Debye dielectric dispersion model from the measured broadband S11, and utilized as the features to create a large dataset by adding various Gaussian noises. Machine learning algorithms were then used to classify glucose concentrations ranging from pure water to 1000 mg/dL. A perfect 100% glucose concentration classification accuracy has been achieved. The study suggests a proposing way to develop the non-invasive glucose detection method using big data machine learning.
